## EA Media Tools 2.3.1 - jaguar

### NVIDIA auto-crop decoding fix

- Auto-cropped NVIDIA jobs now retain generic NVDEC instead of disabling hardware decoding before FFmpeg starts.
- The crop runs through a protected system-memory bridge, then returns to CUDA for scaling, optional tone mapping, and NVENC output.
- The workspace decoder indicator now correctly reports NVIDIA NVDEC for these jobs.
- A real NVDEC failure still retries once with software decoding while retaining the selected NVENC encoder.

### Folder subtitles and movie naming

- Folder mode automatically attaches SRT files that share the complete video basename, such as `Show A H264.en.default.srt` for `Show A H264.mkv`.
- Two- or three-letter language codes set the subtitle language. The `default`, `forced`, and `sdh` tokens set their matching dispositions; `sdh` is reported as hearing impaired.
- Sidecars appear in the subtitle tab immediately and are converted to `mov_text` when the output is MP4.
- A folder-mode source without both a season and episode number is treated as a movie. Smart naming writes it to `converted/Title (Year)/Title.ext` when a year is present.

### Validation

- Verified the corrected pipeline against an H.264 High source on a GeForce RTX 5050 with Jellyfin FFmpeg 8.1.2: NVDEC initialized, CUDA crop/scale completed, HEVC NVENC accepted CUDA frames, and the sample finished with zero decode errors.
- Added regression coverage for CUDA crop bridging, sidecar matching and flags, external-input mapping, closed-caption input coexistence, and movie smart naming.
- Lint, native and compatibility TypeScript checks, unit tests, and Windows x64 production packaging.

[Review changes since v2.3.0](https://github.com/eaforlife/media-converter/compare/v2.3.0...v2.3.1).
